newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Juppe brushes off call to resign.
newsitem.headline: France's Juppe brushes off call to resign.

text.p: French Prime Minister Alain Juppe, whose centre-right coalition took a drubbing from the left in the first round of a parliamentary election on Sunday, brushed off a call by a grassroots activist in his Gaullist party to resign.

"This is not a fairground game of musical chairs. The issue is a choice of policies, a choice of projects for France at the dawn of the 21st century," Juppe replied when asked if he should not step aside in the interest of the party.
"We are calm and determined," the prime minister told reporters at the town hall in Bordeaux, of which he is mayor.
Juppe said he was satisfied with his own score of 38.6 percent on the first round against Socialist challenger Gilles Savary in a constituency in the southwestern city.

"I urge all those who did not vote for us on the first round to think carefully before voting on the second round...I don't think it would be a good thing for France to approach the new century with old recipes which have failed everywhere," he said.

The left-wing opposition polled about 4.5 percent more of the vote than the centre-right in Sunday's first round in what most analysts said was a protest vote against Juppe's austerity policies. Polling institutes said the outcome of next Sunday's decisive second round was wide open.
